properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12, and he said plainly at capture time that he expects this to stay unaccepted — he wanted it on the record, not enacted. Nothing here is settled.

HIS WORDS: "should we have a 'purge' skill. I'm getting pretty happy with how reflow2 is now. There are a lot of still unrealized ideas and gaps that we still should work through, but say I'm happy with the current state of the project - can I just 'purge' all the additional things not yet accepted or built? It is a destructive action, but sometimes I'd like to continue reflow2 without every decision and thing I've submitted."

⭐ THE NEED IS REAL AND ALREADY EVIDENCED. `fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input` records that he pours instructions, ideas, feedback and requirements in as they occur to him. That is the tool working as intended, and its cost is exactly what he is describing: the open list grows faster than anyone decides on it, and eventually it stops being a to-do list and becomes noise.

═══ WHAT THIS WOULD TOUCH, MEASURED 2026-08-12 ═══

  Decision    proposed  104 of 341   carrying 248 edges   2 edgeless
  Requirement proposed   47 of 156   carrying 151 edges   0 edgeless
  Capability  planned    37 of 151   carrying 150 edges   0 edgeless
                        ─────────────────────────────────
                        188 nodes, ~549 edges

🛑🛑 AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHOULD DECIDE THIS: **26 OF THE 47 PROPOSED REQUIREMENTS ARE ALREADY SATISFIED BY SOMETHING.** They are built. Their status simply never moved off `proposed`, because status moves only on the owner's word and nobody went back to say so. A purge keyed on "not yet accepted" would delete more than half its own target set WRONGLY — deleting delivered work along with the speculation.

That is not a hypothesis. It is `req:supporting-is-not-conflict` at scale: during the 2026-07-30 prune that requirement was proposed for dropping as "an orphan in all but name", and checking its single edge revealed it was DELIVERED, by a `realized` capability. The lesson recorded then was "low edge count was read as low value, and for a requirement that has been built, edge count is exactly backwards". One hand-check caught one instance; the same reflex applied in bulk would now be wrong 26 times.

═══ THE PART THAT MAY MAKE THIS UNNECESSARY ═══

⭐ **THE THING HE WANTS MAY ALREADY EXIST, AND IT IS NOT DELETION.** `dec:proposed-requirements-pruned` (accepted, his own word, 2026-07-30) already did this once by hand — nine of twenty-six requirements retired — and its finding is the direct answer here:

> "All are `dropped`, not deleted... `dropped` also stops them raising `unsatisfied_requirement`, so the open list means what it says again."

So the BENEFIT he is asking for — an open list that means something again — is delivered by the STATUS CHANGE. Deletion adds nothing to that and additionally destroys the reasoning. That decision's rationale states the cost of going further: "Deleting them would erase why the surviving rules are shaped as they are, and would let the same captures be re-made next quarter by someone who could not see they had been weighed."

The `retire-from-design` skill already carries dropped-not-deleted as its central distinction. So what is missing is not the ACT; it is doing it in BATCH, and being prompted when the list has grown enough to be worth doing — the same shape as `dec:idea-the-graph-notices-the-record-moved-without-being-asked`, where the tool existed and the trigger did not.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — A BATCH DROP, never a delete. A skill that walks the unaccepted set in classes, proposes a disposition per class, and moves status to `dropped`/`deferred` on his word. Reuses existing vocabulary; nothing is lost; the open list clears. EXPENSIVE: it is 188 nodes, and a batch under one shared reason is precisely what `acknowledge_gaps` already REFUSES by design — "a batch under one shared reason is exactly the erosion the ask-don't-repair rule exists to prevent". So the batching has to be per-class with a stated reason each, which is what made the 2026-07-30 prune trustworthy and also what made it slow.

B — ACTUAL DELETION. What he literally asked for. Cheapest to state, and the only option that genuinely reduces graph size. EXPENSIVE, and the objections are unusually concrete: 549 edges would go with the nodes; the 26 delivered-but-unmarked requirements would go with them; and `dec:ask-not-repair` plus the whole `apply_heal` design exist to stop reflow2 destroying design without a human asserting each case.

C — SNAPSHOT-THEN-CLEAR. Export the design first, then drop hard, on the argument that git holds the memory. EXPENSIVE, and this is the one worth thinking hardest about: a design nobody can query is not memory. `search_design` cannot reach a node that only exists in a file, so "it is in git" means "nobody will ever find it again". The whole point of the graph over documents is that the record is QUERYABLE.

D — DO NOTHING NEW. `retire-from-design` exists and works; the 2026-07-30 prune proves it. What is missing is a nudge when the unaccepted set crosses some size. Free. EXPENSIVE: he has now asked for this, which is evidence the existing route is not discoverable at the moment he wants it.

E — FIX THE UPSTREAM CAUSE INSTEAD. 26 of 47 are stale STATUS, not surplus intent. A pass that asks "these 26 look delivered — accept them?" would shrink the open list by more than half WITHOUT dropping anything, and would make the remaining list honest. Not a purge at all; possibly the thing that removes most of the felt need.

═══ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea rather than used to kill it ═══

The brainstorm skill's own closing rule is that roads not taken are part of the design's memory — "recorded as considered, never deleted... a later session that finds an old idea knows both that it was thought of and that it was not chosen." A purge is the direct negation of that rule. If it is ever built, that rule has to be revisited deliberately rather than quietly broken, because half of what makes this graph worth keeping is that it remembers what was rejected and why.

⚠️ AND A SCOPE NOTE: "not yet accepted or built" is not one population. A `proposed` Decision that is an OPEN QUESTION is not surplus — it is unfinished thinking, and deleting it discards the question rather than answering it. A `planned` Capability nobody will build is different again. Any version of this has to say which of the three it means; the measurement above keeps them apart for that reason.

NOT DECIDED, and expected by its author to stay that way.
properties.name: OPEN — when the owner is happy with the current state, can everything not yet accepted or built be cleared in one deliberate act?
properties.rationale:
Captured on Anthony's explicit instruction to record it without pursuing it — "I expect this one to stay non-accepted, but I did want to capture." That is the funnel working exactly as `fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input` describes, and this node is itself an instance of the thing it proposes purging, which is worth noticing.

The measurement is what makes it worth keeping rather than merely polite: 26 of 47 proposed requirements are already satisfied, so the felt problem is substantially STALE STATUS rather than surplus intent, and option E addresses more of it than any purge would. The 2026-07-30 prune already established dropped-not-deleted and recorded that `dropped` alone restores the open list — so the benefit sought here is reachable without the destruction.
